weakness.title: Missing Tamper Detection for Monitoring Devices
weakness.description: Monitoring devices can be disabled, moved, obstructed or disconnected without the facility being alerted.

extended_description.applicability: Devices that provide monitoring, such as cameras, detectors, door sensors, alarm panels and recorders, with their cabling and power. The tamper resistance of a device's internal hardware belongs to CWE. This entry concerns whether the facility notices that a deployed device has been interfered with.
extended_description.exploitation: An unauthorized person disables or impairs a monitoring device, then enters or acts while it is blind. The facility is not alerted to the interference.

row.details: Monitoring stops working without notice and gives false assurance.
No record exists of what happened while the device was impaired.

row.description: Alert when a device is opened, moved, obstructed or disconnected, or when it loses power or signal.
Monitor the cabling, power and network of monitoring devices, and use a regular signal from each device so that its silence raises an alert.

row.measure: Mount devices out of easy reach
row.description: Install devices out of easy reach and in protective housings.
Keep recorders, panels and controllers in protected rooms.
Check device status regularly, and treat unexplained outages as incidents.

row.reference: NIST SP 800-53 Rev. 5: PE-6(1) Intrusion Alarms and Surveillance Equipment
ISO/IEC 27001:2022, Annex A: 7.4 Physical security monitoring
CWE-1388: Physical Access Issues and Concerns (frontier: hardware-level physical access)
